title: NY State Assembly · District 69
area: Manhattan's Upper West Side and Morningside Heights/West Harlem, including the area around Columbia University

context.text: This is an open seat. Incumbent Micah Lasher is not seeking re-election to the Assembly; he is instead running for the U.S. House in New York's 12th Congressional District. In the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary, Eli Northrup defeated Stephanie Ruskay 60.3% to 39.4% for the open seat. The Republican primary was canceled with no candidate, and Northrup also advanced from the Working Families Party line without appearing on that primary ballot.

summary.text: Eli Northrup is a public defender who has worked for more than a decade in Bronx criminal court and is Policy Director for the Criminal Defense Practice at the Bronx Defenders, where he has led legislative campaigns in Albany. He has not held elected office. He finished second in the 2024 Democratic primary for Assembly District 69, then won the June 2026 Democratic primary for the open seat over Stephanie Ruskay, and describes his platform as defending progressive values, advancing affordability and fighting for working families.

background.text: Northrup was born in Washington, D.C.

He earned a B.A. in psychology from Cornell University (2007) and a J.D. from New York University School of Law (2011); Ballotpedia also lists Georgetown University Law Center (2015), where his survey says he was a clinical fellow.

According to his Ballotpedia survey, he clerked for federal judges on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit and the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, and in law school worked with the NAACP Legal Defense Fund, the Neighborhood Defender Service of Harlem and the Legal Aid Society.

He has worked for more than a decade as a public defender in criminal court and is Policy Director for the Criminal Defense Practice at the Bronx Defenders, where he says he leads a team of advocates working on criminal legal system policy.

He says he worked with legislators in Albany on measures including cannabis legalization, making police records more transparent and reducing the Rikers Island population, and helped launch the Bronx Cannabis Hub, which assists people affected by past drug-law enforcement in obtaining cannabis licenses. City & State described him in 2023 as a public defender who had advocated in Albany for cannabis legalization and bail reform.
According to his campaign platform, he was a founding member and architect of the Communities Not Cages campaign to change New York's sentencing laws.

He announced a run for Assembly District 69 in November 2023 after Assemblymember Danny O'Donnell said he would not seek reelection. He finished second to Micah Lasher in the June 2024 Democratic primary (34.4% to 52.6%), ran on the Working Families Party line, and withdrew from the November 2024 general election.

After Lasher filed to run for Congress, Northrup announced a second campaign for the seat in October 2025, and in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary he defeated Stephanie Ruskay, 60.3% to 39.4%; he also holds the Working Families Party line.

priorities.text: "My vision extends from criminal legal reform to critical issues such as affordable housing, accessible mental health care, and universal child care. I will fight to protect our environment, community gathering spaces, and to ensure that older New Yorkers can stay in their homes and have access to the services that they need."

On affordability: "Affordability is the defining issue facing New York... As your Assemblymember, Eli will be a champion for working New Yorkers in Albany, fighting to advance a bold affordability agenda that delivers real relief to families, seniors, and young people."

On criminal justice: "Having represented people in criminal court for more than a decade, Eli has seen firsthand the deep inequities baked into our system... We can build safer communities while advancing justice, but only if we commit to policies rooted in care, accountability, and shared responsibility for one another."

positions.summary: Supports raising the state minimum wage to $30/hour by 2030 and ending the tipped minimum wage.
positions.quote: $30/hour by 2030: Eli will fight for a minimum wage of $30/hour by 2030.

positions.summary: Supports the New York Health Act to establish a universal single-payer health care system covering all New Yorkers.
positions.quote: Eli will champion the New York Health Act to establish a universal single-payer system. Doing so would cover all New Yorkers and expand coverage to include dental, mental health, reproductive care, and more.

positions.summary: Supports the strongest version of Good Cause Eviction, closing loopholes, and a statewide right to counsel in eviction proceedings.
positions.quote: New York State must enact the strongest possible version of Good Cause Eviction. Loopholes like the LLC Loophole or exclusions for small buildings must be closed.

positions.summary: Supports the Universal Child Care Act to guarantee every family access to early childcare.
positions.quote: Eli will champion the Universal Child Care Act to ensure that every family has access to early childcare.

positions.summary: Supports the Invest in Our New York package to raise taxes on corporations and the wealthiest 1% to fund affordability programs.
positions.quote: Eli will support the Invest in Our New York package, which will raise taxes on corporations and the wealthiest 1% in order to pay for the affordability agenda.

positions.summary: Opposes state and local cooperation with ICE, says ICE should be abolished, and supports the New York for All Act and a statewide right to counsel in immigration proceedings.
positions.quote: In the meantime, New York must stand strong against ICE and Border Patrol 'missions' that terrorize communities and tear families apart... New York for All: Eli will champion this legislation that cements New York's status as a sanctuary state.

positions.summary: Supports keeping Manhattan's congestion pricing program, citing evidence it reduces traffic and raises MTA funding.
positions.quote: Congestion Pricing: Eli will be a staunch defender of New York City's congestion pricing program.

positions.summary: Opposes weakening the Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act (CLCPA), supports a cap-and-invest program, and opposes new fossil-fuel infrastructure.
positions.quote: Defending the CLCPA: Eli will strongly oppose any efforts to weaken, delay, or roll back the CLCPA... Opposing New Fossil Fuels: Eli will fight against new fossil fuel infrastructure of any kind.

researchNotes: Northrup has never held elected office, so there is no official voting or bill-sponsorship record; his positions are documented from his detailed campaign platform and his 2024 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (he had not completed a fresh 2026 survey as of research). His own materials give no family or residence details beyond his birthplace, so none are included.
